# Neural Radiance Field Integration

Also called: Bundle-Adjusting NeRF, Joint Optimization of NeRF and Poses

## Overview
Neural Radiance Field Integration refers to the family of [optimization procedures](#7150-optimization-procedures.md) that simultaneously refine inaccurate camera poses and optimize the parameters of a [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) . It solves the problem of reconstruction failure when initial camera poses are erroneous, which causes [standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) to converge to local minima or produce artifacts . It differs from [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) optimization by treating camera parameters as learnable variables alongside the neural network weights, and from pure pose estimation methods by leveraging the geometric consistency of the learned 3D representation .

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) to compute gradients with respect to both the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) parameters $\theta$ and the camera pose parameters $P_i$ . The rendering equation for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ is:
$$ \hat{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N T_i \left( 1 - e^{-\sigma_i \delta_i} \right) \mathbf{c}_i, \quad T_i = e^{-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j} $$
where $\sigma_i$ and $\mathbf{c}_i$ are the density and color predicted by the NeRF $\mathcal{F}_\theta$ at sample point $i$ [G]. The total loss $\mathcal{L}$ is typically the [Mean Squared Error](#1651-mse-loss-and-psnr-conversion.md) (MSE) between rendered colors $\hat{C}$ and ground truth images $I$ [G]:
$$ \mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \| \hat{C}_i - I_i \|^2 $$
Gradients $\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \theta}$ and $\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial P_i}$ are computed via backpropagation through the differentiable renderer [G]. Camera poses are typically parametrized in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ as a 6D vector $n$ ([rotation](#19376-rotation.md) $\omega$ and translation $t$), which is exponentiated to a transformation matrix $N = \exp(n)$ for composition with reference poses .

## Subtopics

### [BARF (Bundle-Adjusting Neural Radiance Fields)](6872-barf-bundle-adjusting-neural-radiance-fields.md)
Uses a coarse-to-fine frequency schedule for positional encoding to prevent high-frequency noise from misleading the optimizer when poses are inaccurate. Choose when initial pose errors are moderate and computational resources are limited.

### [L2G-NeRF](8671-l2g-nerf.md)
Combines local non-parametric photometric alignment with global parametric geometric alignment to handle large displacements and poor initialization. Choose when initial poses are very poor (e.g., identity) or when large camera movements exist.

### [CBARF](9066-cbarf.md)
Extends BARF with a cascaded [bundle-adjustment](#8540-bundle-adjustment.md) structure and distinct modulation factors for each stage to handle larger initial pose errors (e.g., 30.4° rotation) without overfitting. Choose when BARF fails to converge due to large initial pose deviations.

## Background
The concept of joint optimization of NeRF and camera poses was introduced by . Early work demonstrated that standard NeRF optimization is highly sensitive to initial pose accuracy, often failing with even small errors. Subsequent developments like [L2G-NeRF](#8671-l2g-nerf.md)  and CBARF  addressed limitations regarding large displacements and overfitting, respectively. These methods are primarily used in [Structure-from-Motion (SfM)](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) pipelines where initial pose estimates from traditional methods may be insufficient for high-fidelity NeRF reconstruction.
